title: Targeting C/EBPbeta/SCD1/C16:1 loop-driven macrophage M2 polarization by Bruceine D improves anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in colorectal cancer.
authors: Zhao, Lei; Huang, Wankun; Li, Chengbin; Wang, Qingkun; Han, Yue; Yang, Wenqing; Zhu, Lu; Lin, Zhenhua; Piao, Junjie
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Bruceine D通过靶向C/EBPbeta抑制M2巨噬细胞极化以增强结直肠癌免疫治疗，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作（C/EBPbeta调控SCD1转录）及分子对接/MD模拟，但核心是免疫代谢与药物机制，非TF-DNA结合建模研究，方法应用浅层。
abstract: The immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, particularly M2-like tumor-associated macrophages (TAM), critically contributes to colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Here, we identify Bruceine D (BD), a natural compound, as a potent regulator of macrophage-associated immunometabolism in CRC. BD suppressed tumor progression and enhanced anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (anti-PD-1) immunotherapy efficacy in both MC38 and CT26 syngeneic mouse models without inducing significant systemic toxicity. Mechanistically, BD inhibited M2-like macrophage polarization in THP-1-derived macrophages, bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), and human monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs), while attenuating the tumor-promoting effects mediated by macrophage-conditioned medium. Integrated transcriptomic, metabolic, and mechanistic analyses indicated that BD interacts with CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein beta (C/EBPbeta) and suppresses stearoyl-CoA desaturase 1 (SCD1) transcription, thereby reducing the production of palmitoleic acid (C16:1). In turn, C16:1 maintained C/EBPbeta protein stability, forming a positive feedback loop that sustained M2-associated macrophage phenotypes. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, cellular thermal shift assay, and surface plasmon resonance collectively supported the direct interaction between BD and C/EBPbeta. Multiplex immunohistochemistry analysis of human CRC tissue microarrays further demonstrated positive correlations among C/EBPbeta, SCD1, and the M2 marker CD206 in clinical specimens. Collectively, our findings support the C/EBPbeta/SCD1/C16:1 axis as an important immunometabolic pathway involved in regulating M2-like macrophage phenotypes and suggest that BD represents a promising therapeutic strategy for improving anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in CRC.
abstract_zh: 免疫抑制性肿瘤微环境，尤其是M2样肿瘤相关巨噬细胞（tumor-associated macrophages, TAM），对结直肠癌（colorectal cancer, CRC）的进展及免疫检查点抑制剂耐药性具有关键作用。在此，我们鉴定出天然化合物鸦胆子素D（Bruceine D, BD）作为CRC中巨噬细胞相关免疫代谢的强效调节剂。BD在MC38和CT26同系小鼠模型中抑制肿瘤进展并增强抗程序性细胞死亡蛋白1（anti-PD-1）免疫治疗疗效，且未诱导显著全身毒性。机制上，BD抑制THP-1来源巨噬细胞、骨髓来源巨噬细胞（bone marrow-derived macrophages, BMDMs）和人单核细胞来源巨噬细胞（monocyte-derived macrophages, MDMs）中的M2样巨噬细胞极化，同时减弱巨噬细胞条件培养基介导的促肿瘤效应。整合转录组学、代谢组学和机制分析表明，BD与CCAAT/增强子结合蛋白β（C/EBPbeta）相互作用并抑制硬脂酰辅酶A去饱和酶1（SCD1）转录，从而减少棕榈油酸（C16:1）的产生。反过来，C16:1维持C/EBPbeta蛋白稳定性，形成正反馈环路，持续维持M2相关巨噬细胞表型。分子对接、分子动力学模拟、细胞热位移分析和表面等离子体共振共同支持BD与C/EBPbeta之间的直接相互作用。人CRC组织微阵列的多重免疫组化分析进一步证明，临床标本中C/EBPbeta、SCD1和M2标志物CD206之间存在正相关性。总体而言，我们的研究结果支持C/EBPbeta/SCD1/C16:1轴作为参与调节M2样巨噬细胞表型的重要免疫代谢通路，并提示BD代表一种改善CRC中抗PD-1免疫治疗的有前景的治疗策略。
